newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 19.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 19.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST...
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
LONDON - Advertising and marketing company WPP Group Plc agrees to buy Taiwan-based sales promotion firm Team-Mate Marketing Development & Services Ltd.
MUNICH - Bavaria's Hypo-Bank says it has assigned a "significantly higher" advertising budget to TBWA agency to launch an image study and put together plans for a new campaign.
LOS ANGELES - Golf star Tiger Woods files lawsuit against the Franklin Mint for unauthorised use of his likeness on a commemorative medal it is marketing.

LONDON - Newspapers' share of advertising spending is falling in the world's top five economies, but growth in emerging markets in Asia-Pacific and Latin America is underpinning the demand for newsprint according to Zenith Media, the media-planning and -buying unit of advertising and marketing group Cordiant Plc.
MEXICO CITY - Mexico's new private pension funds spent 1.29 billion pesos ($163.2 million) on advertising between February and May, according to the Reforma newspaper.
ZURICH - Advertising pages in Swiss newspapers fell 7.4 percent in May compared with a year earlier after a 3.3 percent rise in April, according to figures compiled by the WEMF media tracking agency.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

LONDON - British independent television companies Carlton Communications Plc and Granada Group Plc are negotiating to buy British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc's stake in British Digital Broadcasting, the Times newspaper says.
LONDON - The number of European shopping sites on the Internet is expected to reach 15,000 by the year 2001, almost a 10-fold increase from current levels, market research group Datamonitor says.

BONN - Bernd Kundrun, managing director of pay-TV channel Premiere, is to switch to publishing group Gruner+Jahr-Verlags (G+J) in August, Bertelsmann-unit G+J says. G+J denies that Kundrun's move from Premiere has anything to do with negotiations between Bertelsmann and the Kirch group over the future of Premiere, in which both have interests. German news magazines have reported that Kirch has demanded Kundrun's dismissal.
NEW YORK - Mercury Radio Communications LP sold four radio stations in Buffalo, New York to Broadcasting Partners Buffalo LLC for $62 million, Broadcast Partners says.
LONDON - British cable and satellite television company Flextech Plc says it has conditionally agreed to sell its entire 23-percent stake in HIT Entertainment Plc.

BONN - Germany's millions of Turkish residents feel inadequately informed by the media, according to survey findings unveiled by the government. The survey, however, also discovered that around a half only ever read Turkish-language newspapers.

MELBOURNE - Loss-making pay television operator Foxtel says its two shareholders News Corp Ltd and state-owned Telstra Corp are not losing patience with the business and that major changes to the industry might take some time.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS

NEW YORK - R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co strikes back at the Federal Trade Commission with a lawsuit that seeks to block the FTC's crackdown on Joe Camel, the tobacco company's controversial marketing symbol.

FRANKFURT - Carmaker Adam Opel AG, the German unit of General Motors Corp, launches the largest product offensive in its history, offering 26 new models by the end of 2001. Opel says the new models will include eight new small trucks and that six new vehicles will be offered in 1998 alone, including the new compact van Zafira that will be unveiled in September at the Frankfurt car show.
ATLANTA - The Coca-Cola Co is sponsoring a 20-city bus tour from June 19 to July 31 in conjunction with the Boys & Girls Clubs of America for a promotion called the Incredible Summer.
SOFIA - Bulgaria, under pressure to clamp down on mass production of pirated compact discs, brings its first case to court, but the defendant is acquitted for lack of evidence.

LONDON - Britain's Virgin Group is planning to incorporate the Union Jack in its airline's livery after rival British Airways Plc dropped the national flag from most of its aircraft, according to newspaper reports.

PARIS - Electrical appliances company Moulinex says there are no signs of real recovery in consumer spending in France or in western Europe overall. "The climate in France remains grim," says a company spokesman.
SEOUL - Daewoo Motor Co, a unit of South Korea's Daewoo Group, has raised its export forecast to 430,000 vehicles in calendar 1997 from an earlier projection of 400,000.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

PARIS - In the land of "haute cuisine", a survey has shown that French people most like eating quiche, steak and chips, and stew. An IPSOS opinion survey shows 81 percent of French people like quiche lorraine "a lot", making it the most popular dish in France.

TOKYO - Japan, tired of its huge dependency on oil, has found a cleaner source of energy -- sewage. The city of Yokohama says it's turning sludge -- a by-product of sewage that comprises human, domestic and industrial waste -- into "clean energy" by extracting methane gas and using it to generate electricity.

LONDON - Lovers wanting to keep in touch may soon be exchanging telephone tokens. A design student has come up with the idea of a digital token, the size and shape of a lipstick, which can be shared by friends, family and business contacts, reports the New Scientist magazine.

NEW DELHI - Indian cinema owners facing strong competition from TV and home videos are offering consumers improved decor, snazzier projection, smaller theatres for niche audiences and plenty of food and drinks. Of India's 13,000 cinemas, at least 1,000 have already closed due to losses, say industry observers.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's handover to China is to be marked by a Red Dawn. The South China Brewing Company has produced a special "Red Dawn" lager decorated with '97 labels and the red flag of China folding over Britain's Union Jack.

WELLINGTON - New Zealand's Dairy Board is breaking into the competitive Gulf Arab market for processed cheese by injecting the foodstuff into plastic packs moulded in the shape of toys. A spokesman says the move is based on research that indicates "the influence young people in the region have on what their parents put into the trolley".

BONN - Germans ate significantly more soup in 1996 than the year before, possibly indicating a return to austere eating habits linked to higher unemployment,the Federation of German Soup Manufacturers says.
